title: Agent Autoloop: a coding agent that keeps working alone

facts.method: tool's own README and repo page, read on the day of the plan
facts.limits: The catch: you need a recent Node, Git and an agent already signed in, and the CLI is still in Chinese.

scenes.heading: AGENT AUTOLOOP WORKS ALONE
scenes.say: Tired of babysitting your coding agent?

scenes.heading: A BACKGROUND LOOP
scenes.say: It's Agent Autoloop, a background coding agent: it turns a command line agent into a loop on one machine.

scenes.heading: EVENTS, THEN RULES
scenes.say: A schedule, a new issue or an alert becomes an event, and your rules pick which agent handles it and where.

scenes.heading: ONE ROUND, THEN EXIT
scenes.say: The agent works one round and exits, so it isn't standing by and burning tokens while it waits.

scenes.heading: A CARD, NOT A DASHBOARD
scenes.say: When a decision is yours, a card reaches you in Slack, Discord or a desktop notification, and one command resumes it.

scenes.heading: THE CATCH
scenes.say: The catch: you need a recent Node, Git and an agent already signed in, and the CLI is still in Chinese.
Would you let an agent work while you're away? Comment LOOP and I'll pin it.

viewer.job: decide whether a background loop fits how they already run Claude Code or Codex

idea: Agent Autoloop runs a command-line agent in a background loop and only asks when a decision is yours.

claims.text: Agent Autoloop turns a command-line agent into a background loop on one machine, with no server and no dashboard.
A schedule, a new GitHub issue or a production alert becomes an event, and the rules choose which agent takes it and in which folder.
The agent works one round and exits, so nothing is standing by and spending tokens while it waits for a decision.
When the decision is yours, a card reaches Slack, Discord or a desktop notification, and one command resumes the work.
